overview: The two-day period was dominated by Yonghong Song's 20-patch series (v3) enabling exception cleanup landing pads to run when bpf_throw() unwinds, a major step toward C++-style resource cleanup in BPF programs spanning the verifier, x86/arm64 JITs, libbpf, and bpftool. Kuniyuki Iwashima introduced new bpf_tcp_ops hooks for TCP AutoLOWAT receive-queue management, while Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi continued refining the verifier's handling of generic __uninit kfunc output buffers. Hash map performance and memory footprint also improved via independent submissions from Meta and Google engineers.

patches.title: bpf: Accept the compiler's exception cleanup table at program load
patches.author: Yonghong Song
patches.summary: First patch in a 20-part series (v3) that teaches the BPF loader to accept a compiler-generated exception cleanup table alongside a program. When bpf_throw() unwinds the BPF call stack, the kernel can now dispatch designated landing-pad subprograms to release resources such as ring buffer reservations or locks before the exception propagates. The series requires changes across the verifier (CFG walking, landing-pad reachability), the x86 and arm64 JITs, libbpf (static linker, light skeleton), and bpftool. This enables reliable structured error handling in BPF without leaking in-flight resources.

patches.title: bpf: tcp: Introduce bpf_tcp_ops.{enqueue,dequeue}_rcvq().
patches.author: Kuniyuki Iwashima
patches.summary: Introduces two new bpf_tcp_ops callbacks — enqueue_rcvq and dequeue_rcvq — that fire when data is placed on or removed from the TCP receive queue, enabling BPF programs to implement TCP AutoLOWAT (automatic sk_rcvlowat adjustment). A companion kfunc bpf_tcp_set_rcvlowat() allows programs to adjust the watermark directly, and a new BPF_SOCK_OPS_RCVQ_CB_FLAG opt-in controls the callbacks. This allows latency-sensitive applications to tune receive-buffer wakeup behavior without kernel modifications, benefiting workloads like high-frequency trading or network proxies.

patches.title: bpf: Fix generic __uninit kfunc output buffers
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: Fixes a verifier bug where kfuncs annotated with __uninit on their output buffer arguments were incorrectly inheriting initialization state from previous uses of the same stack slot, potentially allowing uninitialized data to escape. The fix tracks raw memory arguments recorded during argument checking and ensures __uninit output slots are always treated as uninitialized write targets. The 11-patch series also adds support for multiple __uninit output arguments per kfunc and tightens read-access checks for helper input/output buffers.

patches.title: bpf: Speed up htab hashing for u32/u64 keys
patches.author: Mykyta Yatsenko
patches.summary: Optimizes the hash function used by BPF hash maps when the key size is exactly 4 or 8 bytes by using dedicated integer-hashing routines instead of the generic jhash path. For common map patterns that use u32 or u64 keys (e.g., PID lookups, socket cookie maps), this removes multi-word hashing overhead and improves throughput on hot lookup paths. The change is safe because the optimization is gated on exact key-size checks at map creation time.

patches.title: bpf: htab: Split htab_elem_lru and htab_elem_pcpu off of htab_elem
patches.author: T.J. Mercier
patches.summary: Refactors the htab_elem structure to separate LRU-specific and per-CPU-specific fields into distinct types, reducing per-element memory overhead for non-LRU non-pcpu hash maps by 8 bytes. A follow-up patch further shrinks elem_size for maps with small keys by omitting the redundant key copy stored alongside the value. At scale, with millions of hash-map entries, this yields measurable memory savings without any change in observable semantics.

patches.title: bpftool: Read ring buffer maps with event_pipe
patches.author: Tianyi Chen
patches.summary: Adds an event_pipe subcommand to bpftool's map handling so ring buffer maps can be consumed directly from the command line and piped to other tools. Each sample is written to stdout as a hexdump or binary blob, making it straightforward to integrate BPF ring buffer output into shell pipelines or monitoring scripts without writing a custom consumer program. A companion selftest validates the new mode end-to-end.

patches.title: bpf: Destroy callee-local dynptrs on subprog return
patches.author: Xu Yunxiang
patches.summary: Fixes a verifier correctness bug where dynptrs created in a subprog and not explicitly released could silently outlive the subprog's stack frame, leaving dangling references visible to the caller. The fix teaches the verifier to implicitly destroy callee-local dynptrs upon subprog return, consistent with the existing treatment of iterators and other frame-local objects. A sibling patch extends BTF pointer lifetime tracking for iterator-owned pointers, and both changes are covered by new selftests.

patches.title: bpf: Reject bpf_skb_output() from return-side tracing
patches.author: Feng Yang
patches.summary: Prevents bpf_skb_output() from being called in fexit or fretprobe contexts where the attached function may have already freed or invalidated the skb argument, which would allow out-of-bounds reads when sampling packet data into a perf/ring buffer event. The fix adds a context check in the helper's kernel-side implementation and is paired with a selftest that verifies the restriction is enforced at load time.
